newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH GDYNIA SHIPYARD SEES SWING TO PROFIT IN '97.
newsitem.headline: POLISH GDYNIA SHIPYARD SEES SWING TO PROFIT IN '97.

text.p: Poland's Gdynia shipyard, preparing to join a planned industrial group, said on Tuesday it expected to swing to a seven-million-zloty net profit in 1997 after losing 90 million zlotys last year.

"Last year, we had a net loss of 90 million zlotys, but if we took into account net results from last year's sales of 10 ships, the loss was only 14 million," Krzysztof Banaszak told a news conference.
He said without elaborating that the 1996 loss was so large because the company changed its auditing methods. In 1995, the shipyard had a net loss of 14.5 million zlotys.
The company, controlled by the state, had sales of 778 million zlotys last year, compared with 526 million zlotys in 1995.
The shipyard has contracts for building 31 vessels worth $1.2 billion, which should it busy until mid-1999, Banaszak said. It is negotiating 36 additional contracts worth $1.4 billion, he added.

He confirmed that the general shareholders' meeting would vote on April 8 on increasing the yard's capital by between 45 and 150.8 million zlotys, or by between 30 and 50 percent of its share capital.

Gdynia's capital increase is likely to pave the way for the creation of the shipyard industry holding group, which would be led by the Szczecin shipyard and also involve Cegielski engine maker and possibly a steel mill, Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek has recently said.
An industrial source, which asked not to be named, said on Tuesday that a large bank was interesed in joining the planned group.
